images.text:
Peter: So where is this place exactly, near the Fair Grounds, isn't it?
Vanessa: Yeah, but don't worry we'll meet at my restaurant and I'll take you there.
Peter: Just to be sure, the tickets are free, right?
Vanessa: No Peter. Yours are double! Yes, the tickets are free. Their facility has a bar and some food stands, but I'm just getting you the tickets. You are coming, aren't you?
Peter: I gladly accept your invitation.
Vanessa: Peter. I envy you sometimes.
Peter: For my winning smile, boyish charm and perfect hair?
Vanessa: No, I'm jealous of your complete lack of social awareness. Is it as freeing as it seems?
Peter: Hahaha. V. I'm just kidding. Relax. It's fair.

Sally: Umm. So, who else is on the team?
Vanessa: I would like four more people if possible. We could ask Denise and Donald, couldn't we?
Vanessa: Unfortunately, They're out of town this weekend.
Sally: Ron and Peggy. They are in town, aren't they?
Peter: Didn't you and Peggy have a falling out ?
Sally: Oh, right!
Sally: Well, there is Becky and Hank. They're really athletic. How many triathlons have they been in?

Peter: We aren't running a triathlon,are we? We are just throwing things at a wall. We don't need Mr. and Mrs health and fitness.
Sally: Hmmm. Who do you suggest Peter? You have a lot of friends, don't you?
Peter: Only you guys. Invite anyone, except Camilla.
Vanessa: Hmmm. Is Camilla's number in my phone?
Peter: Funny!

Intonation of Statements, Short Questions and Question Tags

Statements go down as you progress through the sentence. Short questions go up at the end of the sentence. Tag questions go up at the end of the question when the speaker doesn't know the answer. Tag questions go down at the end of the question when the speaker feels they know the answer.
Practice saying these sentences with the intonation going down or up.
